name: devices
description: Paired machines: presence, announced adapters and capabilities, rename, revoke, and the pairing-approval panel.

aliases.@convex/_generated/api: Convex generated api object; the only import in config/functions.ts

providers: ConvexProvider or ConvexAuthNextjsProvider from the app shell
<Toaster /> from @/components/toast mounted once by the app shell — useToast throws without it, so a mutation failure can never be swallowed silently
notes: No UI-kit dependency: components are native elements plus the class vocabulary in app/globals.css. Dialogs are the platform <dialog>, not Radix.
The slice maps a device status to a semantic tone and stops there; the host's StatusBadge owns the colour.

DevicesPanel.preloaded: Preloaded<typeof api.features.devices.queries.listMine> — optional; omit to query on the client
DevicesPanel.labels: LabelOverride<DevicesLabels> — optional deep override of every user-visible string
DevicesPanel.dateFormat: { locale?, timeZone?, fallback? } — optional; defaults to the runtime locale

PairApprovalPanel._: The consequential screen: it states what approval grants (local actions on that machine) and that the device credential is never shown here nor handed to an AI client. Both live in labels.pairing, so a consumer translates the warning but cannot drop it.
PairApprovalPanel.code: string — pairing code from the agent, usually the /pair route parameter
PairApprovalPanel.preloaded: Preloaded<typeof api.features.pairing.queries.getByCode> — optional; omit to query on the client
PairApprovalPanel.now: number — optional server clock so the first client render matches SSR; advisory, the mutation re-checks expiry
PairApprovalPanel.onApproved: () => void — optional callback after a successful approval
